beba8b17d577: This is the key idea of the whole lesson: in Polish, men have their own numeral. Ask the check question “are they all men?” — we will come back to it on every slide.
dbbea433a5d2: Show that after a numeral the noun stands in dopełniacz liczby mnogiej (genitive plural), and the verb is usually neuter singular: przyszło. Don't go into the variants — they are in the exceptions block.
0e87647c897c: Compare men and animals: trzech kolegów, but trzy psy. Animals are counted like things. This prepares the trap about koty.
baca6eff1ce9: The question word ilu is used only for men. For «how many people» we say ile osób. Ask the students to put the question to their partner: Ilu masz kolegów?
c36af2545f93: Do not demand all cases from the weaker group: the main ones are M./B. (nominative/accusative: dwoje dzieci) and D. (genitive: dla dwojga dzieci). The instrumental (z trojgiem dzieci) is for stronger students. Note that 4 is czworo, not “czteroro”.
09df3e2439ee: Three typical cases: children, a mixed group, and «ludzie» without specifying gender. Ask the students to make up their own sentence about their family: Mam troje rodzeństwa.
587f86220539: Osoba is feminine, so in the mianownik (nominative) we say trzy osoby, pięć osób, even when we are talking about men. In the biernik (accusative) and after prepositions the numeral changes: dla pięciu osób, z pięcioma osobami.
42e22e9f7cf9: Three cases: 4 gives czworo (not czteroro), young animals (szczenięta, kocięta) are counted with collective numerals, and plural-only nouns (drzwi) too. For drzwi you can also say dwie pary drzwi.
